title: A tour of the window
summary: The ribbon, Quick Access Toolbar, formula bar, Name Box, status bar and Backstage view.
objectives: Find the ribbon’s tabs and groups, and the Quick Access Toolbar.
Use the Name Box and the formula bar.
Read Sum, Average and Count in the status bar.
Open Backstage view from the File tab.

slides.h: The ribbon: tabs, then groups, then buttons
p: Across the top is the **ribbon**. Each **tab** (Home, Insert, Page Layout, Formulas, Data, Review, View) holds **groups** of related buttons, labelled along the bottom.

Home has what you use most: fonts, alignment, number formats, Sort & Filter. If you can’t find a button, think about which tab’s job it is: printing lives on Page Layout, protection on Review, freezing rows on View.

visual.caption: The Home tab and its groups

slides.h: The Quick Access Toolbar and the title bar
p: Above the ribbon sits the **Quick Access Toolbar**: Save, Undo and Redo, always one click away. You can add your favourite buttons to it.
The title bar in the middle shows the file’s name. The **AutoSave** switch on the left saves every change automatically when the file lives on OneDrive or SharePoint.

visual.text: Press [[Alt]] in Excel on Windows: letters appear on every tab and button, so you can drive the ribbon from the keyboard.

slides.h: The Name Box and the formula bar
p: Just above the grid, on the left, the **Name Box** shows the active cell, such as D4. Type an address into it and press Enter to jump straight there.
Next to it, after **fx**, is the **formula bar**. It shows what’s really inside the active cell: the formula, not just its result. You can also edit the cell there.

visual.caption: The Name Box and the formula bar for cell D8

check.q: Which part shows the formula behind a cell’s result?
check.explain: The formula bar shows the real contents of the active cell.

why.0: The Name Box shows the cell’s address (or a name), not what’s in it.
why.2: The status bar sums selections; it doesn’t show formulas.
why.3: That holds Save, Undo and Redo.

lecture.title: The bottom of the window, and File

slides.h: Sheet tabs and the status bar
p: Along the bottom are the **sheet tabs**, plus the ⊕ button to add a sheet.

The **status bar** below them does quick maths on whatever you select: select some numbers and it shows their **Average**, **Count** and **Sum**, with no formula needed. On the right are the view buttons and the zoom slider.

visual.caption: Select D2:D6 and the status bar shows Average, Count and Sum

p: The **File** tab doesn’t open a ribbon; it opens **Backstage view**: a full-screen menu for saving, opening, printing, sharing and exporting.
Press **Esc** or the back arrow to return to your sheet.

visual.caption: Backstage view: everything about the file itself

check.q: You select ten numbers. Where can you see their total without writing a formula?
check.explain: The status bar shows Sum, Average and Count of the selection.

demo.intro: Step through the window, one area at a time.

frames.say: The **ribbon**: tabs across the top, groups of buttons below. Home holds the everyday tools.
The **Name Box** (left) shows the active cell. The **formula bar** shows what’s inside it.
Select a range and the **status bar** does instant maths: Average, Count, Sum.
**File** opens Backstage view, where you save, print, share and export.

quiz.q: Which tab holds Freeze Panes and Zoom?
quiz.explain: Viewing tools live on the View tab.

quiz.q: What does the Name Box show when you click cell F12?
quiz.explain: It shows the active cell’s address.

quiz.q: You want to jump to cell X500. Fastest way?
options: Type X500 in the Name Box and press Enter
quiz.explain: The Name Box jumps anywhere instantly.
File opens Backstage view for saving, printing and sharing.

quiz.q: What does AutoSave need to work?
options: A file saved on OneDrive or SharePoint
quiz.explain: AutoSave saves continuously to cloud files; for files on your laptop, save with Ctrl+S.

points: The **ribbon** has tabs, groups and buttons; think about which tab’s job a tool is.
The **Name Box** shows and jumps to addresses; the **formula bar** shows what’s really in a cell.
The **status bar** gives Sum, Average and Count of any selection.
**File** opens Backstage view: save, print, share, export.
recap.cheat: Name Box = where you are. Formula bar = what’s really there. Status bar = quick maths.

cards.back: The real contents, such as the **formula**, not just its result.
